output.name: Hasket

anatomy.part: hook at the top of the spindle, the curl at the top of the shaft
whorl, the weighted disc at the centre of the spindle
sharp tip at the bottom of the spindle, where the shaft tapers to a point
spun yarn leaving the rim of the whorl, on the trailing arc

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, Mother Hesk was spinning the new thread that would have held the sky close. Her drop spindle slipped from her fingers in the wind and went up after the cut end, still turning. Tulma, the whorl, spun thread as it climbed, and Kesin, the hook, caught on nothing. Hesk has waited for it ever since, the way a woman waits for a child gone down to the rocks. She keeps count of the yarn it spun on the way up. Ennu says the thread is nearly long enough to reach the islands. Tavo says it is not, and laughs when he says it. Aun says nothing. He mends a net. When the thread is long enough, the old woman says, the spindle will drop down the string and the sky will come home. Until then we spin our wool short and tie the ends. Mind your hands on the spindle when the wind is up.
output.verse:
Hesk's spindle turns high
still spinning the cut thread down
the wind keeps the count

problems: The blind guess ('a long diagonal stroke with a curved hump arc, no clear object') describes the lines but does not identify a drop spindle. Nothing reads as a spindle at a glance: the whorl is not drawn as a disc, and the yarn reads as an arbitrary hump.

Star placement is roughly correct. Hook star 83895 is at the top-left end of the shaft (127,168), tip star 78527 at the bottom-right end (296,341), and whorl star 80331 sits on the shaft at about (231,274). End-of-yarn star 75458 at (403,317) is correct.
The yarn star 77277 at (329,245) is on the arc, but the trailing yarn is a sharp polyline with a kink at that star, not a spun-yarn curve leaving the whorl rim.

The figure is a thin stroke-and-hump outline, not a recognisable silhouette. The gold lines trace the star-to-star path, and the blue arcs around the hook and whorl look like decorative guide ellipses rather than the object's outline.
Labels collide and are clipped: 'hook at the top of the spind' and 'sharp tip at the bottom of t' are truncated, and the whorl label runs across the shaft and the yarn line.
The shaft is tilted about 45 degrees and the whole form is small and off-centre in the frame.
judge.advice: Redraw as a recognisable drop spindle. Use a single straight shaft from hook 83895 at (127,168) down to tip 78527 at (296,341), with a small curl at the hook end. Mark whorl 80331 at (231,274) as a filled disc: draw a short ellipse centred there, perpendicular to the shaft, about 20 px across. Draw the yarn as one smooth arc starting on the whorl rim, rising over to the peak near 77277 at (329,245), and descending to end star 75458 at (403,317), with no kink at 77277. Remove the blue guide ellipses and let the gold lines be the silhouette itself. Shorten the labels, place them outside the figure with leader lines, and make sure none are clipped. Centre the whole figure in the frame.
